sources.title: Hunter Schafer on Art, Love, Ambition—and Life Beyond 'Euphoria' (GQ Global Creativity Awards cover, 'Queen of the Youth')
sources.speaker: Hunter Schafer, profiled by Emma Carmichael over two days at her Los Angeles home; includes quotes from Dan Stevens, Tilman Singer and stylist Dara Allen
sources.locator: Article body: opening house tour; 'I can't just wing this shit' paragraph; childhood/art paragraphs; 2020 breakdown and truck drive; Rosalía confirmation; Angus Cloud; 'very intentional' de-centering of transness; final 'reason to live' paragraphs
sources.excerpt: "I can't just wing this shit. I really have to be intentional about the way I'm moving in the world." ... "I'm pretty sure I needed it as a way to externalize what I didn't feel I could externalize with myself," ... "I have to be in control and decide how to survive this," ... "It has not just happened naturally by any means. If I let it happen, it would still be giving 'Transsexual Actress' before every article ever." ... "I've gotten offered tons of trans roles, and I just don't want to do it. I don't want to talk about it." ... "I am a proper Capricorn. I want to control everything." ... "You can really find joy in making stuff," Schafer says. "I find it to be a reason to live."
sources.context: Longest profile on record (she later called it 'two like four-hour sessions', S05). Written at a career lull between Hunger Games and Cuckoo. Stevens: 'She absolutely fizzes with creative energy... It's just like it's got to get out of her.' Singer: 'She's relaxed, but she's not casual.' Allen: 'obsessive understanding about art and fashion and culture' and 'She's down to clown.' The journalist describes 'the sunny, people-pleasing young advocate' giving way to protective cynicism. She cries when Angus Cloud comes up. Confirms Rosalía relationship (fall/winter 2019) with Rosalía's permission.

sources.title: Hunter Schafer Steps Into the Light
sources.speaker: Hunter Schafer, profiled by Haley Mlotek; phone quotes from Zendaya and costume designer Heidi Bivens
sources.locator: Opening journal-box scene; 'turn inward' pull quote and paragraph; Method-acting paragraph; anger paragraph; Zendaya and Bivens quotes; closing 'pockets of special, intense relationships' paragraph
sources.excerpt: "When your exterior world and your body and your self are not in line with who you are, you turn inward. And my theory is that I built a really rich inner world until I started feeling like myself in my body." ... "I've already spent a lot of my life trying to be someone I'm not," ... "For the first 20 years of my life," she says, "there were times I got so angry, to the point I could feel it in my body." ... "Even before I graduated high school, I've just been grinding, grinding, grinding to make a life for myself so that I can do what I want to do, and now I finally have space to reflect." ... "She just took whatever pain she had, and she translated it into such a beautiful performance."
sources.context: Conducted October 2021 during season 2 filming, in her rented Hollywood apartment near the set, as she digitally archived a lifetime of journals. She says the story of her life 'begins in my late teens' and that 'mostly everything before I transitioned is a blur'; cries when asked about her mother. Zendaya describes being 'as much of a big sister as I could.' Bivens calls her professionalism 'unparalleled' with 'a sort of selflessness that helps her get into the character.' She was not in therapy when Euphoria began and is now; uses a therapist's 'box' visualization to close Jules at day's end.

sources.title: Hunter Schafer: "Trying to Feel Seen Has Been the Project of My Life" (Allure September 2020 cover)
sources.speaker: Hunter Schafer, interviewed over Zoom by Brennan Kilbane
sources.locator: Truck-drive opening; 'projection of Jules' and Teen Titans Raven paragraph; 'I'm messy' paragraph; 'T-word' paragraph; 'creating the identity of a person' paragraph; pull quotes
sources.excerpt: "I have no idea what I'm doing — just riding the wave that life is handing me and trying to be okay and keep my shit together. I think whatever presence I have, in the public-figure world, presents itself as something more collected, but I'm messy." ... "Even right now, I have to filter what I say, because more often than not I've found that when I say the T-word, whatever sentence that is becomes a headliner," ... "When you think about it, [my work] has this common thread of creating the identity of a person," ... "That's been the project of my life," she says. "Just trying to feel seen and learn how to see others correctly."
sources.context: Spring/summer 2020, after the COVID shutdown of season 2 and her cross-country drive to her sister's in North Carolina. She describes Jules as 'one part of me' using the Teen Titans image of Raven splitting into ten colored selves. The writer notes her 'slow, considered, and slightly raspy' voice and that trans questions dominate 'nearly every interview she does.' She says Black Lives Matter allyship should include work that is 'not Instagrammable.'

sources.title: Hunter Schafer on 'Blade Runner 2099,' Queerness, and Her Gender-Affirming Surgery (ELLE November 2026 cover)
sources.speaker: Hunter Schafer, interviewed in London by Lotte Jeffs
sources.locator: Paragraphs on pastor parents and 'being in service'; 'fucking mess' paragraph; action/'being in your body' paragraph; 'flatter' gender paragraph; bottom-surgery disclosure in the hotel tea room; 'perception' paragraph; closing childhood dance-party memory
sources.excerpt: "I do think it's truthful to say I was a fucking mess for the first chunk of my twenties, up until a few years ago." ... "The reason I like action so much is you don't have to think that much," Schafer says. "It's just being in your body." ... "I'm a woman. I'm a girl," ... "I just had bottom surgery in December, which was amazing, and I love it so much." ... "They defy the introvert because I want to be around them, touching them, all the time. When I'm in love, that's how I feel. I want to be with you all the time." ... "People who are not thinking about perception at all. And I think about perception all the time. It's a big part of my job. It's not cool at all." ... "I was so shy and so scared to dance in front of other kids, I was crying. I was so nervous and scared," she says. "I still did it, trying to smile, but I kept being like, 'No.' I think that's what I was at my core before this job broke me open."
sources.context: Late-summer 2026 interview in Grosvenor Square and a hotel tea room while she was in London for a friend's wedding (the writer infers Zendaya's). She says Christianity gave her childhood 'structure and purpose' and that 'being in service' or 'making things for something bigger than yourself' still drives her, 'for the poetry.' She describes her teens as 'really angry at the world.' Recovery from the December 2025 surgery limited her to about 150 steps a day; she is 'happy being on her own because there are so many thoughts to think.' Names Fran Lebowitz, Björk and Patti Smith as cool. Says she has not had a relationship longer than two years.

sources.title: Hunter Schafer: Polyamory, Cheating & Fame (Full Episode) — Call Her Daddy
sources.speaker: Hunter Schafer, interviewed by Alex Cooper; her sister Hannah is in the room
sources.date: 2024-08-07 (episode aired; this full-episode YouTube upload is dated 2025-02-28)
sources.locator: Audio segments re-transcribed with Whisper small.en on 2026-10-29 (cache files yt/seg/chd-*.txt): 00:02:30-00:03:40 (drag version of self); 00:11:00-00:13:30 (hated North Carolina; 'who I am'; access to joy); 00:20:30-00:23:00 (art as what she was put on earth to do); 00:26:00-00:28:40 (parents, intuition); 00:38:00-00:45:00 (fame as tool, paparazzi day, Hunti); 01:09:00-01:14:00 (men, monogamy, cheated on); 01:22:30-01:24:30 (fell in love with the craft); draft note (2026-10-29): article quotations use contiguous spans of the Whisper transcription; the 'pretty easy access to like joy' fragment omits a preceding repeated 'like a', and the 'it has everything to do with that person' fragment begins after a spoken 'And, and, and'.
sources.excerpt: "the image that I put out into the world, like on Instagram, whatever, is like very much like the drag version of who I am. And it's like an image that I've put together to like give to the world." ... "afflictions with life is I have never been able to really help but be who I am" ... "I'm so thankful that I have not really been given a choice to be anyone but who I am" ... "I've always had like a like a pretty easy access to like joy, I think." ... "I know that that's what I was put on this earth to do was to like make stuff." ... "I don't personally gain anything from it. If anything, it's just, like, made existing in public a little harder as a socially anxious person, but, like, but it's an amazing tool to, like, get what I want and to make what I want happen." ... "the famous hunter, is kind of like, my drag, and having those be separate is so important for my fucking sanity" ... "it's part of why the relationship ended is, is I, I got cheated on for the first time" ... "that like fundamentally changed me as a person. And it was this whole process of like realizing that cheating has nothing to do with you at all." ... "all the answers are inside of me"
sources.context: Recorded days after she accepted Blade Runner 2099 and a day before leaving for Europe; she calls the week 'crazy.' Every excerpt above was checked against a Whisper small.en re-transcription of the audio on 2026-10-29 (the YouTube captions had 'I put together' where the audio says 'I've put together'). She also says: she 'fucking hated North Carolina' growing up but loves returning now; middle school was hardest; she came out to friends first; the Euphoria per-episode paycheck was 'more money than I've ever seen'; she describes 'the pressure cooker that I sort of placed myself in' as a teen pouring everything into art; she would walk away from fame if she could keep the money; her relationships run on standby and friendships have ended over her absences; her first relationship was with a trans woman; Fike was her first monogamous relationship and first with a cis man; she says she went through his phone; she says 'I'm here to talk about my truth' while wanting to protect what happened between them. Name spellings in the Whisper output ('hunter, shaper', 'hunty') were normalized from the captions.

sources.title: Hunter Schafer & Lorde | The A24 Podcast (2022) ('Divine Frequency with Hunter Schafer')
sources.speaker: Hunter Schafer in conversation with Lorde (Ella Yelich-O'Connor), recorded in Hollywood during Euphoria season 2 filming
sources.locator: Audio segments re-transcribed with Whisper small.en on 2026-10-29 (yt/seg/a24-*.txt): 00:06:00-00:08:30 (drawing since childhood); 00:15:00-00:17:00 (shy, casting); 00:22:00-00:26:00 (words vs images; co-writing; 'most cathartic'); 00:33:00-00:35:30 (ADHD, Capricorn systems, 'free spirit'); 00:37:00-00:39:00 (frequencies; trans-girl love story). Method-class remark at 00:26-00:28 is caption-level.; 00:26:45-00:27:16 (captions): the casting director put her in a month-long Method class in New York and she dropped out after two weeks 'because it is so hardcore'; the article states this without quoting it.
sources.excerpt: "something parallel to an addiction was formed with drawing" ... "I'm less shy now because acting has sort of really broken me out of my shell. But definitely, I was really shy." ... "I think of myself as not that great with words which is why I draw and and paint and stuff like that because that feels so much easier than trying to articulate myself with these shit words" ... "we did it in like a week the first draft" ... "it was it was definitely like the most cathartic artistic experience i've had so far in life" ... "I have pretty intense ADHD" ... "I didn't think I was that way" ... "I want to be a free spirit" ... "and go with the flow" ... "the closest thing I have to a spirituality is like is like I believe in people like riding Frequencies"
sources.context: Two-hander with a friend, so speaker attribution needs care: Lorde is the Scorpio who says she does not journal and does not make friends easily; Schafer is the Capricorn with 'pretty intense ADHD' who maps things in notebooks. When Lorde said she thinks of Capricorns as 'needing systems to make it through,' Schafer answered 'I didn't think I was that way' and said she had pushed the trait away for a while 'because I was like, no, I want to be a free spirit and go with the flow' (Whisper hears 'redirected that trait' and 'free spirit'; the YouTube captions had 'rejected that trait' and 'a spirit'; the sense is the same). Excerpts above follow the Whisper re-transcription. She also says the casting director put her in a Method acting class in New York that she quit after two weeks (caption-level), that the 'baby doll era' is a trans-girl rite of passage ('dress like the 5-year-old girl that you never got to be'), and that she wants a two-trans-girl love story with 'Marvel level CGI.' Nylon (S45) confirms the release date and title.

sources.title: Q&A: A NC Teen And Her Parents On The Transition From Male To Female
sources.speaker: Hunter Schafer (17), Katy Schafer and Mac Schafer, interviewed by Jess Clark (WUNC)
sources.locator: Q&A sections: first realization; coming out as gay in seventh grade; eighth-grade anxiety; third coming-out attempt; fashion-camp heels; pronouns; nonbinary exploration
sources.excerpt: Hunter: "I've always had this persistent need for femininity and expressing that—like ever since I was a teeny, tiny toddler." ... Katy: "The anxiety level in Hunter was so apparent that I know that we could not continue kind of turning an eye or not listening. I felt like we were reaching a crisis point, because we had kind of lost our kid." ... Mac: "I think that's when everything became real." ... Hunter: "I just wish that some people could see more to me than that right away" ... "I do like people to know that I'm not a cisgirl because that's not something that I am or feel like I am. I'm proud to be a trans person."
sources.context: Only family testimony on record. Katy says the draw to the feminine was there 'maybe from 18 months on' (Catwoman, Hawkgirl, a pink dress at preschool) and that she first told Hunter 'just because you're an artist and just because you like pretty things, that doesn't mean you're transgender.' Mac, a Presbyterian pastor, describes saying yes to heels at a fashion-design camp while 'everything in me was going no, no, no.' Hunter says puberty brought 'dread and wrongness,' that she learned about trans identity from open-minded friends and the internet, and that at 17 she was 'exploring the nonbinary part of myself' and 'swinging back to somewhere in between.'

sources.title: Why I'm Fighting North Carolina's Anti-Transgender Bathroom Law (Teen Vogue op-ed)
sources.speaker: Hunter Schafer (first-person essay at 17)
sources.locator: Opening paragraph and third paragraph
sources.excerpt: "Every time I use a public bathroom, I have to make a choice: Do I break the law, or do I disregard my comfort and face the risk of harassment and violence?" ... "I did this not only in the hope of reversing it but also to represent other transgender youth in North Carolina who are as hurt as I am, and to raise awareness and acceptance for transgender individuals."
sources.context: Written weeks after joining the ACLU/Lambda Legal suit against HB2. The stated motive is representation of other trans youth, not personal grievance alone. Later profiles (S09, S14, S13) show her reframing the decision as something she did 'because I could' from a position of privilege.

sources.title: Hunter Schafer, Model and Activist, on the Bathroom Bill (W Magazine Capricorn feature)
sources.speaker: Hunter Schafer (19), interviewed in New York by W Magazine
sources.locator: Paragraphs on Chase Strangio's message, depositions, 'Hell, yeah', tokenization, the activist label, Central Saint Martins plans
sources.excerpt: "Hell, yeah," she said. "Hell, yeah." ... "I knew I should take the opportunity, especially coming from a background of privilege," ... "I'm being tokenized, in a way, so it's this weird sort of in-between platform, where it's a privilege, but it's also not doing my community the best," ... "The grit of Hood by Air, the narratives of Vaquera, and the craftsmanship of Thom Browne."
sources.context: Between the HB2 repeal (March 2017) and Euphoria. She describes months of depositions she had not anticipated and says she would do it again. She had interned at Vaquera sewing garments, walked Helmut Lang, Miu Miu and Marc Jacobs, and was bound for Central Saint Martins that fall. The 'activist' label already sits uneasily: 'her own activism is maybe not enough to make her comfortable with calling herself an activist.'

sources.title: From Transgender Activist to Runway Model (New York Times Style 'Up Next')
sources.speaker: Hunter Schafer, interviewed by The New York Times
sources.locator: 'Claim to Fame', 'Big Break', 'Next Thing' and 'Turning Point' sections (read via Wayback Machine capture)
sources.excerpt: "What I'm trying to do in all senses is deconstruct our idea of gender, and use the privileges that come with looking like a model to bring attention to that," ... "I don't know if I would call myself an activist, as much as someone who's just vocal about being trans, which sometimes can feel like activism, because just existing as a trans person can often be hard enough, particularly for people of color or people who don't pass,"
sources.context: She used the courtesy title Mx. at the time, lived in a Bushwick loft, planned a Manhattan studio and gallery for trans artists with Teen Vogue grant money, and faced a hormone decision that could change her measurements and bookings ('I'm probably going to make art about it soon'). Shows the 2018 nonbinary-leaning framing that she later moved away from (S04).

sources.title: Enthralled by 'Euphoria'? Hunter Schafer Knows Why (It's Because of Her)
sources.speaker: Hunter Schafer, phone interview with The New York Times
sources.locator: Q&A answers on similarity to Jules, high school ('my default is to be internal'), the activist label, nonbinary identity, the psych-ward episode and therapist gatekeeping (Wayback Machine capture)
sources.excerpt: "I didn't act out on it, but I certainly desired to be treated a certain way in order to affirm my femininity." ... "I can't say I lived the way these characters do, just because my default is to be internal and stay home. Making artwork was my saving grace in high school." ... "I have sort of let go of the idea that I need to do the one or the other — and just let myself be."
sources.context: The writer calls her 'the sunny Schafer, 20.' She says Jules's 'desire for romance and normalcy and love' and wish to be treated 'like a woman' (with quote fingers) matched 'that point in my life.' She defines activist as a daily community organizer and says she took the label on because people told her she was one. She recalls needing a therapist for a year to confirm to doctors she was female before hormones, 'which is nuts.'

sources.title: Hunter Schafer on Playing an Unprecedented Character
sources.speaker: Hunter Schafer, interviewed by Chloe Schama (Vogue)
sources.locator: Intro and Q&A: 're-formation' quote; casting answer; 'toxic idealization of men' answer
sources.excerpt: "I'm trying to find a new rhythm as to how I'm going to externalize my artistic energies. It's a moment of re-formation." ... "I could have never really seen myself taking on such a performative art practice, because I'm pretty shy, but I went in and gave it a run, and they asked me to come back and come back again." ... "I identified with that shift, in terms of having a toxic idealization of men, and then letting that fall away and putting more value in relationships with femme people who you trust and love deeply."
sources.context: Two weeks after wrapping season 1. The writer notes she seems to want to steer away from her activist past toward the work. She says she was 'definitely intimidated' by the pilot's graphic scenes and asked where Jules's story was going before committing; 'I don't think I even told them I wasn't coming' about Central Saint Martins.

sources.title: Trans Superstar Hunter Schafer on Her Moment of 'Euphoria'
sources.speaker: Hunter Schafer, interviewed by Daniel D'Addario (Variety)
sources.locator: Paragraphs on auditioning ('F–k it; why not?'), 'altered the way I think', HB2 and the activist label, role-model question
sources.excerpt: "As a trans person I worked really, really, really hard to figure out who I was and solidify that and take hold of it. The idea of having to put that aside and create this new person is scary. But it's also really exciting to me, continuing to morph and to evolve." ... "I don't feel prepared or mature enough, but I think it'll be interesting to see what happens over the next few months of the show airing. It might not really be up to me anymore."
sources.context: The writer describes her as 'light and airy as her idealist character.' She frames the HB2 suit as 'a place of privilege in my transition' where she 'could handle making myself visible,' adds 'But I don't think that makes me an activist,' and says 'the internet saved me' via transition-timeline videos.

sources.title: Hunter Schafer on Euphoria, world-building and trans fantasy (Dazed Infinite Identities issue, interviewed by Rowan Blanchard)
sources.speaker: Hunter Schafer, interviewed by friend Rowan Blanchard with Thora Siemsen (Dazed); conversation held December 2018
sources.locator: Intro paragraphs (Rookie, HB2 'because I could'); Q&A on casting skepticism, world-building pull quote, separate journal for Jules, clothes as affirmation, pressure to represent
sources.excerpt: "No matter what I've worked on or what art practices I've delved into, they've always been an attempt to world-build. Whatever was not in my direct vicinity that I needed in order to feel fulfilled, I tried to create." ... "I just got a separate journal for Jules, so I'm not journalling in my own journal as Jules any more." ... "I think earlier in my transition, where Jules is right now, I definitely relied on clothes and dressing-up as a way to affirm myself." ... "I was putting pressure on myself, worrying about how many facets of the trans community would not be represented by this one singular trans character."
sources.context: Pre-premiere. She recalls her first reaction to the casting call: 'This is a white, cis, straight man writing what seems like a really intense show about a lot of different intersections of various identities that aren't directly related to him.' Describes a five-hour first meeting with Levinson. On HB2: 'When I took my place as a plaintiff... I did that because I could... before that it had always been my intention to be an artist.' Rookie taught her 'making art to a deadline and with an audience in mind.'

sources.title: Euphoria's Hunter Schafer Gives Interview About Jules (first-paparazzi profile)
sources.speaker: Hunter Schafer, interviewed by Maxwell Losgar (Cosmopolitan) in a car after a press day
sources.locator: Paragraphs on first paparazzi, 'purposeful' quote, Rookie/Tavi, HB2 'example', the modeling check, the 2018 Instagram sketch, Levinson coffee meeting
sources.excerpt: "I don't feel like I'm changing as much as the other elements of my life are changing," she says. "I want to be very purposeful and not let that change me, but it's a scary thought." ... "My gender was so influenced by a need to be used by men." ... "By the time I graduated, I had this nice little check and I was like, okay, this is my ticket to New York," ... "Sam really ripped himself open to write this story,"
sources.context: She says she 'was not as cool' than Jules in high school and 'snuck out one time'; that Tavi Gevinson found her Instagram after a birthday tag and invited her to contribute to Rookie; that she joined the HB2 suit 'to be an example of who the bill was affecting'; and that 'since middle school, all I wanted was to be in a city, particularly New York.' The January 2018 sketch caption about men is quoted by the writer from her Instagram.

sources.title: Hunter Schafer on Euphoria, modeling and fame (Marie Claire September 2019 issue)
sources.speaker: Hunter Schafer, interviewed by Marie Claire
sources.locator: Paragraphs on modeling money, auditioning, social-media distance, role-model weight
sources.excerpt: "I worked with some of my favorite designers on the planet, but I never really made a lot of money. I was living paycheck to paycheck." ... "It's really wild to be at this new level of visibility," she says. "It's something I'm still adjusting to and trying to understand." ... "I think that [term] has a lot of weight to it," she says, admitting she's unsure she can live up to their expectations.
sources.context: Describes 'at least five' callbacks, a 'slow burn' modeling career, 'a pretty solid distance' from social media after the premiere, and 'In a way, filming Euphoria was like a year of college.' The writer characterizes her parents as conservative, which conflicts with her own later description of 'the chiller side of Christianity' (S05).

sources.title: TIME100 Next 2021: Hunter Schafer (tribute by Zendaya)
sources.speaker: Zendaya
sources.locator: Full tribute text
sources.excerpt: "She makes everyone in her orbit feel seen." ... "Her ability to fearlessly navigate the darkest and most emotionally taxing scenes with such a haunting rawness and emotional honesty leaves me speechless." ... "She visualizes something and knows exactly how it can be realized."
sources.context: Promotional tribute by a close friend and co-star, written after the Jules special episode. Useful for the specific traits a long-term collaborator chose to name (emotional honesty; making others feel seen; visualizing and executing), not as neutral assessment.

sources.title: Hunter Schafer on co-writing 'Fuck Anyone Who's Not a Sea Blob' (Awards Focus Emmy-season interview)
sources.speaker: Hunter Schafer, interviewed by Awards Focus
sources.locator: Answers on dependence on acting, five-hour coffee meeting, 'most cathartic', 'fiending', words vs imagery
sources.excerpt: "I hadn't realized that over the course of season one I had developed a dependence on acting." ... "it was the most cathartic, artistic experience I've ever had." ... "It might have catalyzed something reminiscent of an addiction because I am going to be fiending for that sort of catharsis for the rest of my life." ... "I don't naturally feel like I take to words that well. I prefer imagery and other forms of storytelling, but it all goes hand in hand."
sources.context: She says she 'had to do some backpedaling because Jules is 17 and I'm 22,' that the therapy-session material drew on 'my own personal ways of thinking about trans-ness,' and that making narratives that do not yet exist in mainstream media is 'part of my mission within my career.' Describes the cast as 'like a family... I feel really held by them.'

sources.title: Hunter Schafer says Jules' special Euphoria episode helped her get through "the worst depression" (Capital FM report of her i-D interview)
sources.speaker: Hunter Schafer, quoted from i-D by Katie Louise Smith (Capital FM)
sources.locator: Quoted paragraphs from the i-D interview
sources.excerpt: "I was in a very fucking raw place, you know, it was the summer of 2020. Probably coming out of the worst depression I've ever had, and needing somewhere to put all of that energy." ... "When I say that episode really became a lifeline, I mean it,"
sources.context: Secondary copy of an i-D interview (the i-D page itself was not opened). She says the episode was a chance 'to put some shit on TV that has not been on TV as far as like, what's actually going on in young trans people's heads beyond, Oh, I'm scared what people are gonna think because I'm trans. Like, real, spiritual, philosophical… Who am I? What does this all mean?'

sources.title: Hunter Schafer says depression was a catalyst for her transition (Attitude report of her AnOther AW23 interview with Viviane Sassen)
sources.speaker: Hunter Schafer, quoted from AnOther Magazine by Attitude
